verdict: A, B and C are mathematically distinct functions of the same physical variable rho. A and C saturate (low-density growth rho and sqrt(rho) respectively); B grows as sqrt(rho) at high density and does not saturate. C is the same rational saturation template as A under the variable transform y=sqrt(rho/rho_crit), but not the same law in rho. B is a separate power law. The corpus shows a BE -> von Neumann -> chain rule -> per-mode n(n+1) -> mode activation chain as the mediator, but no single consistent derivation links both BE exponents to one Gamma. E proportional to g gives exp(g/a0); E proportional to sqrt(g) gives exp(sqrt(g/a0)); the latter is explicitly supported by the grid-action and microphysics files. No source shows E proportional to g uniquely forcing A, or E proportional to sqrt(g) uniquely forcing B or C without extra assumptions.
falsification: This reading falls if a versioned primary source provides one dimensionally consistent, explicit common derivation from the same microphysics to one Gamma(rho), while resolving the 31942821 conflict between A/B and exp(g/a0)/exp(sqrt(g/a0)).
